page: Google Cloud Platform c4n-standard-96-lssd is an x86_64 architecture instance from the Network Optimized server family, equipped with 96 dedicated vCPUs and 360.0 GB of memory, yielding 3.75 GB per core. The server includes a dedicated local storage array composed of 16 local NVMe SSDs totaling 6442 GB of disk capacity. It does not incorporate hardware GPU accelerators and is provisioned with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

The system combines high-density processor core allocation with high-capacity direct-attached NVMe storage. Because the storage is physically local, the configuration avoids network storage latency penalties for high-IOPS applications. The absence of accelerator hardware and specialized matrix extensions means processing efficiency derives entirely from raw dedicated x86_64 compute execution across its 96 virtual cores.

This hardware profile delivers solid resource efficiency for workloads requiring balanced multi-threaded performance and massive local storage throughput. The instance is suited for distributed database clusters, NoSQL datastores, real-time analytics engines, caching nodes, and batch processing systems that depend on fast scratch disks and parallel computation.
description: Google Cloud Platform c4n-standard-96-lssd is an x86_64 instance from the Network Optimized family, designed for compute-heavy and disk I/O-intensive deployments. It features 96 dedicated vCPUs, 360.0 GB of system memory offering 3.75 GB per core, and a bundled storage subsystem of 16 local NVMe SSDs providing 6442 GB of high-throughput disk capacity. The configuration includes no discrete GPU hardware and zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses. Combining a high core count with extensive high-speed local flash storage eliminates remote storage bottlenecks, delivering dependable performance for sequential and random disk operations. Consequently, the server provides an effective platform for enterprise database workloads, in-memory datastores requiring fast checkpointing, high-throughput ETL pipelines, and distributed analytics frameworks.
